purpose: Teach: 腹筋/退治/金髪/トウモロコシ/ねずみ/かぼちゃ/ウイスキー/サウナ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが腹筋運動を毎日されたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father used to do sit-ups every single day.
lines.style: Soft, remembering voice. Gaze slightly distant. Speaks with the gentle certainty of someone recalling a fact he's held for decades. Warm, no bitterness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お庭の虫退治を引き受けてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you used to take care of all the insects in the garden, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Bright, affectionate correction. Leans in slightly with the warmth of teasing. Eyes crinkling. Her voice carries the ease of someone who knows him completely and is reminding him what matters.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは金髪の方と国際交流をされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father used to go on cultural exchanges with foreign friends.
lines.style: Same gentle distance. Slightly slower pace on the second memory. Quiet pride underneath. Still reaching back, still turning it over in his mind.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、夏はトウモロコシを焼いて下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in summer you used to grill corn for us, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Playful insistence. A small laugh underneath. Not correcting him sharply—more like she's reminding them both of something sweeter. The 'dear' carries real affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがお家のねずみを退けて下さったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father drove the mice out of the house.
lines.style: Same wistful register. Pause before the next memory. His voice carries the weight of accumulated years. Patient. Unrushed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、秋にかぼちゃを煮てらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And in autumn you used to cook pumpkin stew for us, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, gentle insistence. Her voice is softer now—still playful but with the accumulated tenderness of shared seasons. Meeting him halfway.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがウイスキーを嗜まれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, my father enjoyed a good whisky.
lines.style: Final memory, slightly slower. The gentleness has deepened. His voice carries the acceptance of time passing. Still reaching back. Still kind.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、温泉でサウナに入られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you used to take saunas at the hot springs, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Softest yet. Her voice is intimate now, almost conspiratorial. Eyes full. The 'dear' is the warmest it's been. She's not correcting anymore—she's holding him close.
